Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

theoryforge (development version)

Upgrading from the previous release (0.6.0)

Changed results

  • tf_check() and every report use rigour checklist 2.0, so scores and statuses can change. The bundled panic network moves from 84.8 to 87.3 and the weak example from 12.0 to 2.2.

  • Under checklist 2.0, parsimony no longer loses score or warns for declared auxiliary assumptions. An assumption added for an anomaly fails it unless a prediction it protects, other than the anomaly, is corroborated, where any passed protected prediction cleared it.

  • Under checklist 2.0, non-redundancy scores 1 or 0 by the redundancy screen’s flags, where it scored 1 minus the highest similarity.

  • Under checklist 2.0, mean severity uses the claim-form rubric for a prediction without a declared severity, which it left out, and causal testability counts mediates and moderates, where it counted only causes, increases and decreases.

  • tf_check() reports an item with nothing to assess as n/a with a NULL score and leaves it out of the aggregate, so an empty theory scores 0 where it scored 26. The report gains coverage after aggregate_score.

  • Every function but tf_validate() and the builders reads as empty a collection held as a mapping or a single string, a named list such as Map() returns included, where it read the values or the string as entries. unname() restores the entries.

  • tf_implications() reads mediates and moderates as directed edges and associates as bidirected ones, where it ignored them and so could assert independencies the theory denies. Its record gains criterion, n_bidirected, feedback and inseparable.

  • The causal_dag view of tf_diagram() writes mediates and moderates as -> edges and an association as a <-> b, which it left out, and quotes an id that dagitty or Graphviz split or misread, so the independencies dagitty derives from it can change.

  • tf_compile_sem() ends with a block fixing at zero the covariance of two exogenous or two terminal constructs the theory leaves unrelated, which lavaan frees by default. Pairs with a moderator keep lavaan’s defaults, and deleting the block restores them all.

  • tf_compile_sem() writes a moderator’s main effect, where it wrote only a comment and gave the moderator no path to the outcome.

  • tf_compile_sem() renames, with a comment for each, construct ids that lavaan would refuse or misread, such as c-arousal, which lavaan read as arousal, and puts i_ before an indicator name that lavaan would refuse, such as 7_point_likert_rating.

  • tf_compile_sem() writes a control character or one above U+FFFF in a comment as <U+XXXX>, where a line feed in an id ended the comment and lavaan read the rest as a model line.

  • tf_appraise_amendment() treats a prediction under a new id as renamed when a dropped prediction has the same statement and type, where it matched by id alone, so verdicts can change. Its result gains nine fields after the first four.

  • tf_appraise_amendment() reports a new prediction that cites no proposition as underived, and one derived only from the propositions of the prior theory and protected by no new assumption as an articulation. Neither makes an amendment progressive or keeps it from degenerating, where any corroborated new prediction did.

  • In tf_appraise_amendment(), a prediction counts as corroborated only when no outcome refutes it, dropping a corroborated prediction blocks a progressive verdict and an assumption added for an anomaly is ad hoc unless a new prediction it protects, other than the anomaly, is corroborated.

  • tf_read() and tf_read_corpus() return every YAML sequence as a list, where they returned a sequence of scalars as a vector, or a string for one element, so relation: [increases] adds no edge, and maturity: [draft] fails tf_validate() and no longer makes the gate advisory.

  • tf_read() and tf_read_corpus() read a file as UTF-8 in any locale, where, outside a UTF-8 locale, they stopped a YAML file at the first character the locale could not hold and so refused it or, with a warning, dropped the rest.

  • tf_read() and tf_read_corpus() read unquoted y, Y, n, N, 1,000, a lone . and the .na forms as strings, where they read logicals or NA, so an NA that 0.6.0’s tf_write() wrote to YAML reads back as text such as ".na.real".

  • tf_read() and tf_read_corpus() read a YAML integer beyond R’s integer range as a double, where they read NA. A mapping’s own key wins over a merge key written before it, where the merged key won.

  • tf_write() keeps 15 significant digits, where it rounded numbers to four decimal places in JSON and seven in YAML, so a severity of 0.49996 written to JSON read back as 0.5.

  • tf_tokens() and every function that compares or names text fold accented Latin letters, which they dropped. They keep Greek, Cyrillic and other scripts, which they deleted. Redundancy scores, landscape matches and indicator names such as muller_scale can change.

  • tf_landscape() no longer matches on words of the theory’s title, words such as ‘theory’ and ‘model’ or words in the keywords of more than max_token_share of the records, 0.5 by default. max_token_share = 1 lets corpus-wide words match again.

  • tf_redundancy_check() gains overlap, the overlap coefficient, after similarity and also flags a pair whose overlap reaches 0.85 when both definitions hold three or more tokens, such as a definition contained in another.

  • A number or logical in a text field reads as "", where label: Yes printed as TRUE. An unquoted numeric id such as id: 2026, which tf_validate() refuses, therefore reads as empty, and references to it no longer resolve.

  • A mapping in a text field reads as "", where it read as its first value, so from: {a: c1} no longer makes an edge.

  • A string array written as a mapping, such as measurement: {a: x}, reads as empty, where its values counted.

  • A relation, type, maturity or formal-model type outside its allowed values reads as absent and prints as an empty label, so a formal-model type such as bayesian no longer passes formalisation.

  • Every function but tf_validate(full = TRUE) ignores a string-array entry that is not a nonempty string, so measurement: [""] no longer counts in a theory read from JSON or built in memory, and derives_from: [~] fails the derivation check, which it passed.

  • A text field holding only Unicode whitespace, such as a no-break space, counts as empty, where it counted as present, so the checklist no longer credits it and tf_validate() refuses it in a required field.

  • tf_check() decides each threshold item from its rounded score and sums severities in plain double precision, where R’s extended accumulator let a borderline mean severity pass on one platform and warn on another.

  • tf_litmap() keys a reference that holds a DOI by the DOI, lower-cased and without its resolver prefix, so spellings of one DOI make one co-citation node, labelled in lower case, where they made several.

  • tf_litmap() and tf_landscape() key a keyword or reference that is a whole number by its decimal string, where they turned 100000.0 into 1e+05.

  • tf_new_evidence_dois() recognises DOIs written as doi: 10..., DOI 10..., doi.org/10..., https://www.doi.org/10... or percent-encoded and ignores a trailing full stop, comma or semicolon, so fewer candidates count as new.

  • Three bundled example theories change, and so do their documents, their diagrams and the amended example’s simulation and lavaan syntax. The panic predictions state their point values and tolerances, the amended panic example adds a proposition and the modality-switching example records bounds, an outcome and a sampling plan for pred2.

  • tf_example_names() also returns openalex-panic-2026.corpus.yaml, second in the list, so the names after it move one place.

Changed interface

  • The yaml package is required at version 2.3.8 or later.

  • tf_validate(full = TRUE) checks every required field, type, enum and pattern of the schema and reports a string-array entry that is not a nonempty string, where it checked part of the schema, so a theory that passed can fail.

  • tf_validate() refuses a collection written as a single value or a mapping with <key> must be a list, where it accepted both, except that it already refused a single value, or a single entry written as a mapping, for constructs, propositions or predictions.

  • tf_check() and tf_appraise_amendment() refuse a passed other than TRUE, FALSE, NA or null, where passed: "true" read as a failure.

  • tf_check() refuses a prediction severity that is infinite or outside [0, 1], where one above 1 inflated the aggregate, beyond 100 for a severity of 7, a negative one lowered it and an infinite one made it infinite.

  • tf_preregister(), tf_dossier(), tf_report(), tf_render_report(), tf_osf_push(), dry runs included, and the rigour and development_roadmap views of tf_diagram() stop when tf_check() refuses a severity or passed, where they returned output.

  • tf_simulate() stops with simulate diverged at step <step> when the trajectory diverges, the initial state included, where it returned NaN or Inf rows.

  • tf_simulate() refuses a negative, fractional or logical steps and a dt that is not a finite number greater than 0, where it ran a zero, negative or logical dt or a logical steps and truncated a fractional steps.

  • tf_simulate() refuses a k, damping or init that is not a single finite number, where it ran a logical value or a numeric-string init and returned rows of NaN or Inf or of the wrong length.

  • tf_implications() refuses a mediates or moderates proposition that names an undeclared construct or closes a cycle, which it ignored. Its refusal of a cycle names the cycles option.

  • tf_compile_sem() refuses two constructs, two indicators of one construct or a construct and an indicator whose lavaan names collide, which it wrote without a warning.

  • tf_litmap() and tf_landscape() refuse a min_link that is not a positive integer, where they truncated a fraction, read "2" as 2, gave an empty map for NA and treated 0 as 1.

  • tf_litmap() and tf_landscape() refuse a corpus without a records list or with its records keyed by id, as in a named list, where they analysed keyed records and returned an empty map without records.

  • tf_litmap() and tf_landscape() refuse a record that is not a mapping, where they stopped with an unrelated error, except that they counted a null record or a sequence as a record without keywords.

  • tf_litmap() and tf_landscape() refuse a keyword or reference that is a logical, a fraction, a nested value or an integer of 2^53 or more, where an unquoted NO became "FALSE".

  • tf_fetch_corpus() refuses a response without a results list, which it read as no results, and stops with OpenAlex request failed with HTTP <status> on a refused request, where it returned an empty corpus.

  • tf_fetch_corpus() sends the OPENALEX_API_KEY environment variable, when it is set, as an API key, where it sent none. Pass api_key = "" to send no key.

  • tf_osf_push() stops with OSF upload failed with HTTP <status> when OSF refuses an upload, where it reported the upload as completed, and for a 409 names overwrite = TRUE.

  • tf_read() and tf_read_corpus() refuse a repeated key with (<path>) Duplicate map key: '<key>', where they accepted one in JSON. They also refuse a file holding only [].

  • The causal_dag view of tf_diagram() refuses the ids node and graph, which dagitty reserves.

Changed output

  • tf_preregister() writes Derivation references resolve, where it claimed Derivation chain verified. It gives the version and the implied independencies and lists under each hypothesis its assumptions, rivals and test record and marks a tested one already tested.

  • tf_dossier() adds a test record and the evidence, gives the checklist coverage, names the failed blockers and sets each declared severity beside the rubric’s value, with a note when it exceeds the rubric’s by more than 0.2.

  • The nomological_net view of tf_diagram() draws an association without arrowheads.

  • The pipeline and workflow views of tf_diagram() give each outcome of a prediction tested more than once a node of its own, labelled with its date, where Graphviz merged them and showed only the last result.

  • tf_compile_sem() adds comments on its target, lavaan::sem(), on feedback loops that may not be identified and on constructs with a single indicator.

  • tf_dossier(), tf_report(format = "html") and the rigour view of tf_diagram() mark an item with nothing to assess as n/a, and the development_roadmap view leaves it out and labels each step with its checklist 2.0 criterion.

  • tf_preregister() and tf_dossier() head the severity values Severity (pre-data rubric of claim form), and the severity view of tf_diagram() is titled Pre-data riskiness. The values are unchanged.

  • In every report, the citation of precision becomes Meehl (1967, 1990a), that of risk_severity Popper (1959); Meehl (1967, 1990b) and that of parsimony Lakatos (1970); Meehl (1990a), where they were Meehl (1967, 1990), Mayo (2018); Meehl (1990) and Forster & Sober (1994); Lakatos (1970).

  • citation("theoryforge") names the Comprehensive R Archive Network (CRAN) as publisher and gives the DOI CRAN assigned, https://doi.org/10.32614/CRAN.package.theoryforge, where it gave the Zenodo concept DOI, https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21229964.

  • tf_report(format = "html") escapes every value it writes, where markup in a theory id or another field, such as a<b&c, reached the HTML raw.

  • tf_render_report() keeps double quotes and backslashes in title, where quotes became apostrophes and a backslash stopped Quarto or became an escape. It uses the default for an empty or NA title.

  • tf_simulate() with the default method = "euler" warns when its steps depart from the exact solution by more than 5 per cent, and its record gains method, ignored and opposed after init.

  • tf_litmap() and tf_landscape() warn, under the default method = "components", when one theme holds more than half the linked keywords.

  • tf_landscape() returns max_token_share, field_tokens and phenomenon_tokens after theory_id, and each theme gains focal_terms and alternative_terms, the words behind its matches, after status.

  • tf_fetch_corpus() gives each record a doi after its id and returns source before records, recording where, when and how the corpus was fetched.

  • tf_validate() reports a required text field of the wrong type as <field> must be a string, where it called it missing.

  • tf_write() writes a string array holding one string as an array, where it wrote a scalar that failed the package’s own schema.

  • tf_write() writes NA as null, where JSON had the string "NA" for a missing number and YAML the .na forms, and writes YAML logicals as true and false, where it wrote yes and no.

  • tf_write() writes to JSON each array of scalars read from YAML one entry per line, as Python does, where it wrote the array on one line.

  • tf_osf_push() encodes in full a filename that holds a %XX sequence, which it left unencoded, treats an empty node as absent and uses the default for an empty filename.

  • tf_simulate() trajectories and tf_embedding_redundancy() cosines hold 0 where they held a negative zero, which jsonlite wrote as -0.

New features

  • tf_simulate() gains method = "exact", which propagates the linear system by its matrix exponential (Moler & Van Loan, 2003) and so has no step-size limit.

  • tf_implications() gains cycles = "sigma", which derives the independencies a cyclic theory implies by sigma-separation (Bongers et al., 2021), valid when each feedback loop has a unique equilibrium.

  • tf_post_data_severity() computes how severely a bounded prediction passed its test (Mayo & Spanos, 2006), from new optional prediction bounds and outcome estimate and se. tf_dossier() reports it, and the checklist ignores it.

  • Predictions accept an optional test block with the planned sample size, alpha, smallest effect of interest and power, which tf_preregister() lists in a Sampling plan section. tf_add_prediction() gains test and severity.

  • tf_litmap() and tf_landscape() gain method = "simple_centres", the co-word clustering of Coulter et al. (1998) and Cobo et al. (2011), which gives bounded themes with their centrality, density and strategic-diagram quadrant. tf_litmap() also gains min_theme_size, max_theme_size and max_df.

  • tf_litmap() gains min_cocitation, a threshold for the co-citation map alone that defaults to min_link, and tf_lit_diagram() gains max_edges, which draws only the strongest edges.

  • tf_fetch_corpus() gains api_key, sent only in an Authorization header, and max_records, which pages past the first page, as OpenAlex allows only with a key.

  • A saved OpenAlex corpus of 150 works on panic disorder, openalex-panic-2026.corpus.yaml, is installed under CC0 with the example theories (see tf_example_path()). The package also installs the corpus schema, at system.file("schema", "corpus.schema.json", package = "theoryforge").

  • tf_osf_push() gains overwrite, which adds a new OSF version of an existing file of the same name.

Minor improvements

  • tf_litmap() and tf_landscape() count pairs in linear time and tf_lit_diagram() writes a large map in one pass. tf_landscape() skips the co-citation map it does not use. Results are unchanged.

  • A live tf_osf_push() deposit uses the curl package in place of httr.

Fixes

  • tf_read() and tf_read_corpus() read a JSON file that begins with a byte-order mark, where they stopped outside a UTF-8 locale and warned within one. They no longer warn about a missing final newline in YAML.

  • tf_validate(full = TRUE) no longer stops with subscript out of bounds when a collection entry is a scalar, and tf_implications() and tf_simulate() accept two constructs without ids, which they refused as duplicates.

  • tf_fetch_corpus() reads a response only as JSON, where a response that named a local file or a URL made it read that file or download that URL.

  • The theory schema installed with the package compiles under strict JSON Schema validators such as Ajv, which refused its comment keyword.

Deprecated

  • The default method = "euler" of tf_simulate() will change to "exact" in the next minor release. Pass method = "euler" to keep the current trajectories.

  • The default method = "components" of tf_litmap() and tf_landscape() is planned to become "simple_centres". Pass method = "components" to keep the current themes.

Documentation

  • The documentation of tf_severity() gives its 0.25 directional discount as the package’s convention and describes it as a pre-data ranking of each prediction’s claim form, where it cited Mayo (2018), whose severity is a property of a test and its data.

  • The four prediction types are defined in the schema, ?tf_add_prediction and the methodology article, and the schema marks risk_score and severity_at_test as informational fields that no function reads.

  • ?tf_simulate and the methodology article state when the Euler steps diverge, what the model leaves out and that, being linear, it cannot show bistability (Robinaugh et al., 2024).

  • The documentation no longer says that a cyclic theory implies nothing testable or that dagitty rejects its export, and ?tf_implications and the Developing and testing article warn that a conditional implication tested on fallible measures is rejected too often (Westfall & Yarkoni, 2016).

  • ?tf_compile_sem calls the syntax a starting point for a fit, and the Developing and testing article no longer says that the panic network’s syntax can be passed directly to lavaan::sem(), since its feedback loop leaves the model unidentified.

  • The methodology article quotes the checklist’s criteria, no longer says that a theory passing every item scores 100 and calls its thresholds defaults, where it called them calibrated. It says that the derivation chain checks only that predictions cite declared propositions and that causal testability checks only that a directed relation is present, where its table promised graph reachability and a DAG with derivable implications. It no longer says that a field can override the weights and thresholds in its own copy of the checklist, which no function reads, and says that recombined item scores are not comparable with the default aggregate. It explains that the aggregate is compensatory and that the lexical screen cannot detect empirical redundancy (Rönkkö & Cho, 2022), describes the mechanism item as the share of propositions whose mechanism field is filled in and says that tf_embedding_redundancy() takes a threshold of its own.

  • The documentation describes the landscape statuses as a count of the registered accounts that address a theme, so that a crowded theme calls for predictions that discriminate between them, where it called a crowded theme a redundancy risk. The literature article says that connected components put nearly every keyword of a real corpus in one theme.

  • The schema and ?tf_add_assumption define added_for as the id of the prediction whose anomaly an assumption answers, where the help called it a reason. The Get started article’s example sets protects, where it misused added_for.

  • The literature article’s recipe for turning a scopusflow corpus into a theoryforge corpus keeps one node per cited work, where it split a work into several nodes and left co-citation maps and keyword themes empty.

  • ?tf_fetch_corpus and the literature article describe OpenAlex API keys, which replaced the polite pool that mailto selected, and warn that OpenAlex writes keywords with a language model and changes them over time.

  • The Developing and testing article calls the output of tf_preregister() the hypotheses section of a preregistration, to be completed with the design, sampling plan, analysis plan and inference criteria (Bosnjak et al., 2022), where it called it suitable for deposit.

  • ?tf_diagram and the Developing and testing article say that the venn view draws only the first three constructs, where the article said it took each construct’s boundary conditions.

  • ?tf_render_diagram says that, with as = "widget", the venn, rigour and severity views are returned as a browsable HTML object, where it called every result an htmlwidget.

  • The theory schema no longer promises version gating, draft-stage downgrades or form profiles, which the package does not implement.

theoryforge 0.6.0

CRAN release: 2026-09-01

  • New tf_implications() derives the testable implications of a theory’s causal subgraph. It reads the causal propositions as a directed graph, checks that the graph is acyclic, and returns the basis set of implied conditional independencies: one claim per pair of constructs with no causal relation between them, conditioned on the parents of both, in the notation dagitty prints. That set is the shortest complete statement of what a causal theory forbids in data, so it is what a study can be designed to refute. The package cited the derivability of those implications in its own checklist and derived none of them. A cyclic graph has no basis set and is refused with the cycle named, which is what happens to the bundled panic-network example and its amended version. A theory with no causal relations comes back with an empty set and no error. The Python twin gains theory.implications(), returning the same records in the same order. The derived sets were checked against dagitty and ggm, which sit in Suggests for that purpose and whose tests skip when they are absent.

  • A fourth example theory ships with the package, modality-switching.theory.yaml, and it is the worked example for tf_implications(). Both panic-network fixtures are cyclic, so until now every bundled theory showed only what the function refuses. This one states the modality-switching effect in grounded conceptual processing: sensorimotor experience with a concept drives activation of the modality-specific perceptual system, which raises the cost of switching modality between consecutive trials and eases conceptual access, as lexical familiarity with the word form does too. Five constructs and four causal propositions give an acyclic graph with a fork and a collider in it, and a basis set of six conditional independencies, confirmed against dagitty and ggm. The panic fixtures stay as they are: a feedback loop is legitimate theory, and the refusal is worth seeing as well, so the Developing and testing article now shows both outcomes.

  • New tf_example_names() and tf_example_path() reach the theories and the literature corpus bundled with the package, mirroring example_names() and example_path() in the Python twin, so the README quick start runs straight after remotes::install_github() with no clone.

  • tf_validate() refuses an unrecognised top-level field. A misspelt collection key such as predicitions: was dropped without a word, taking its whole collection with it and moving the aggregate score and the gate. The schema’s additionalProperties was set to match, so a third-party validator agrees.

  • Four further refusals replace a silently wrong answer. tf_read() and tf_read_corpus() no longer accept a top-level YAML sequence of mappings, a shape that used to read as a document with every collection empty. tf_simulate() refuses duplicate construct ids, which produced two different but equally plausible trajectories from one file. tf_check() refuses a non-numeric prediction severity, where it used to coerce one, and tf_validate(full = TRUE) reports the same file as invalid, so the scorer and the validator agree about it. tf_embedding_redundancy() refuses a pair of unequal-length vectors, naming the constructs and the lengths, where it used to recycle the shorter one.

  • An enum field written as a YAML sequence, such as theory_form: [network], is now refused. %in% unboxed the one-element list, so the file validated in R and was refused in Python.

  • tf_check() and tf_dossier() record checklist_version, the version of the checklist whose weights and thresholds produced every number in the report, so two reports written against different checklist revisions are no longer silently comparable. tf_simulate() echoes back k, damping and init alongside dt and steps, so a recorded trajectory can be reproduced from what the record itself reports.

  • The causal-testability criterion now describes what it computes. It asserted acyclicity and never checked it. The criterion and the methodology article now state that the export is emitted as written, that it is not verified acyclic, and that the shipped panic-network example is in fact cyclic. No score, gate or status changed. The check the criterion once implied now lives in tf_implications(), and it can refuse a graph outright instead of quietly rescoring it.

  • Every file the package writes goes through one LF-only, UTF-8 writer, so the R half no longer emits CRLF where the Python half emits LF. tf_write() forces UTF-8 as its sibling writers already did, and a failed quarto render no longer returns its output path as though it had succeeded.

  • The network adapters carry the same 30-second timeout as their Python counterparts, and both languages reject a per_page outside OpenAlex’s documented 1-200 range before making a request.

  • Every vignette now turns console colour off and fixes the console width while it renders. pkgdown passes the calling terminal’s colour support into its build subprocess, and the Get started vignette’s failure path therefore published the tf_validate() error with its bold and yellow escape sequences showing as literal text around the words Error and the exclamation mark.

  • inst/WORDLIST is read at last: spelling joins Suggests and a tests/spelling.R runs the check under R CMD check.

theoryforge 0.5.0

  • The development_roadmap view is rebuilt around a theory hub carrying the title, the aggregate score and the gate. Items are ordered blockers first and then by weight, each labelled with its ordinal, the checklist criterion and whether it blocks the gate, with visible edges down the blockers and the advisory items set three abreast.
  • The three SVG chart views (venn, rigour, severity) now declare a width and a height alongside their viewBox, so each renders at its natural size wherever it is embedded. Without an intrinsic size a chart was stretched to the width of its container, and since the three views have different natural widths the same declared 13px label came out at a different size in each one.
  • The venn discs take the construct-border teal for their outline in place of the former navy, which fell below the 3:1 contrast floor for graphical objects on a dark page and left the figure close to invisible under the dark theme.
  • The bundled panic-network fixtures give the three constructs distinct boundary conditions, so the venn view drawn from them shows where construct scopes diverge, where it used to put a zero in six of its seven regions.
  • All of the above are mirrored byte for byte in the Python twin.
  • Documentation: the Get started vignette shows what tf_validate() returns and demonstrates the failure path, and the development article runs tf_osf_push() in its default dry-run mode, where it was previously withheld.

theoryforge 0.4.0

  • The DOT diagram views are redesigned for content and legibility. Every view opens with a shared Meridian style prelude (Helvetica type, role-coloured rounded nodes); labels wrap so nodes stay narrow; workflow and pipeline nodes carry the id together with the relation or type, where a bare word stood; the development roadmap stacks its items in a single column; and the theme landscape colours themes by status. Every view fits a documentation column. The intermediate representation stays byte-identical to the Python twin’s.

theoryforge 0.3.0

  • New tf_render_diagram() renders the digraph views without leaving R: a DiagrammeR widget for the viewer and R Markdown, or a standalone SVG string with as = "svg". It accepts a theory or a raw DOT string, so tf_lit_diagram() output renders the same way; the three SVG chart views pass through unchanged, and causal_dag is refused with a pointer to dagitty. The rendering packages (DiagrammeR, DiagrammeRsvg, htmltools) are in Suggests, so the deterministic core stays dependency-free, and rendering sits outside the cross-language parity contract. The articles now show each digraph rendered beneath its intermediate representation.

theoryforge 0.2.0

  • The severity chart is re-laid out: bars start just past the longest row label and each value trails its own bar. The diagram intermediate representation for tf_diagram(type = "severity") changes accordingly, and it stays byte-identical to the Python twin’s.
  • Documentation: the articles now show the provenance, development_roadmap, pipeline and co_citation views, the embedding-redundancy screen, tf_validate(full = TRUE) and the remaining build verbs, and a new section covers rendering and depositing.

theoryforge 0.1.0

First public release. The package provides a reproducible workflow for building, developing and testing scientific theories, with behaviour pinned by a shared specification (API_SPEC.md) so the R and Python twins return identical verdicts and byte-identical diagram intermediate representations.

  • Core: theory-object input, output and structural validation; a 12-item rigour checklist with a weighted aggregate score and a blocker gate; diagram intermediate representations (nomological net, provenance, causal DAG); and a deterministic lexical construct-redundancy screen. Where the schema expects an array of strings, a nonempty scalar string is read as a singleton list (API_SPEC.md section 4), so natural YAML such as derives_from: p1 yields the same rigour verdict and gate as the Python twin; an empty or whitespace-only scalar counts as absent.
  • Workflow modes: a builder API with auto-logged provenance (BUILDING); an operationalised severity rubric and preregistration export (TESTING); and a Lakatosian progressive-versus-degenerating amendment appraisal (DEVELOPMENT).
  • Literature layer: a deterministic bibliometric mapping (tf_litmap, tf_landscape, tf_lit_diagram), a parity-exempt OpenAlex corpus adapter, and a deterministic, dependency-free check for DOIs not yet cited by a theory (tf_new_evidence_dois), for use with a search from any source, including the companion scopusflow package. tf_lit_diagram() lists the valid types in its unknown-type error, matching tf_diagram().
  • Testing and review: lavaan model-syntax compilation (tf_compile_sem) and a reviewer-facing audit dossier (tf_dossier).
  • Simulation, reporting and deposit: a deterministic dynamical-system runner (tf_simulate), a Quarto report wrapper (tf_render_report), an opt-in embedding redundancy screen (tf_embedding_redundancy), and an OSF deposit adapter (tf_osf_push, dry-run by default). tf_osf_push() percent-encodes the filename component of the upload URL, keeping the dry-run request identical to the Python twin’s.
  • Cross-language determinism: the literature layer and the amendment appraisal sort with radix (codepoint) ordering regardless of locale, matching the Python twin for mixed-case keywords and ids.
  • Metadata: citation("theoryforge") and the About article read the package version from the package metadata.
